security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden executable payloads in the single SKILL.md file. The external command alerts are Markdown code fences and inline SDK names, and the network and environment alerts are placeholder Azure configuration examples. Users should still apply least-privilege controls when enabling Azure agent tools.

remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to scope code, web, OpenAPI, MCP, SharePoint, and file-search tools before use.

remediation.issue: Environment examples do not include handling guidance for credentials and endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note to avoid committing or logging project endpoints, tenant details, and Azure credentials.

content.user_title: Build Azure AI Projects Apps in Python
content.value_statement: Azure Foundry developers need clear Python patterns for projects, agents, tools, and evaluations. This skill gives concise examples for azure-ai-projects workflows and client choices.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install azure-ai-projects and azure-identity for Python projects.
Demonstrates AIProjectClient authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and a project endpoint setting.
Compares native AIProjectClient workflows with the OpenAI-compatible client.
Provides examples for agents, threads, messages, runs, connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, evaluations, async clients, and memory stores.
Lists supported agent tool classes, including code interpreter, file search, Bing grounding, Azure AI Search, OpenAPI, MCP, memory search, and SharePoint.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not implement a complete application or command-line tool.
The referenced support files are not included in this package.
Examples require valid Azure credentials, project permissions, connections, and model deployments.
Preview SDK APIs may change, so users must test against their installed package version.

use_cases.title: Prototype Foundry Agents
use_cases.description: Plan a first Python agent that creates a thread, adds a message, runs the agent, and reads the response.

use_cases.title: Map Project Resources
use_cases.description: Review how to list Foundry connections, deployments, datasets, and indexes before building application flows.

use_cases.title: Design Evaluation Workflows
use_cases.description: Use the evaluation examples to plan quality checks for model behavior inside an Azure AI project.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Foundry Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the steps for authenticating an azure-ai-projects Python client with DefaultAzureCredential. Include required environment variables and safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a minimal plan for creating an Azure Foundry agent with a model deployment name from the environment. Include cleanup guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tools and Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an agent workflow that uses file search and memory stores. Explain required Azure connections, permissions, and cleanup tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure AI Projects architecture for agents, runs, evaluations, and external tools. Identify permission risks, missing validation, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to connect to a Foundry project and create an agent.
output: Set the project endpoint and model deployment settings first.
Authenticate with DefaultAzureCredential and confirm project permissions.
Create the client, create the agent, run a thread, then delete test resources.

output_examples.input: A team wants to choose between native Foundry APIs and an OpenAI-compatible client.
output: Use AIProjectClient when project resources, connections, agents, and evaluations matter.
Use the OpenAI-compatible client for familiar chat completion calls inside Foundry.
Document any tool permissions before enabling web, OpenAPI, MCP, or SharePoint access.

output_examples.input: An engineer needs guidance for async project operations.
output: Use the async project client with a context manager.
Plan cleanup for temporary agents, files, memory stores, and test data.

best_practices: Confirm project endpoint and model deployment settings before using examples.
Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential instead of embedded secrets.
Clean up test agents, files, and memory stores after experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets into prompts, notebooks, or example files.
Do not enable code, web, MCP, or OpenAPI tools without permission boundaries.
Do not assume preview SDK examples work across versions without testing.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python examples for Azure AI Projects, including clients, agents, tools, project resources, evaluations, async usage, and memory stores.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance; users must execute and validate any code separately.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Real runs require Azure permissions, a valid project endpoint, and a deployed model name.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for Microsoft documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use official Microsoft documentation for current SDK details, service limits, and release changes.

faq.question: What security care is needed?
faq.answer: Use least-privilege credentials and restrict code, web, OpenAPI, MCP, file-search, and SharePoint tool access.
